subject: MAP: POC environment & connectivity timeline (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex White <alex@healthbridge.io>, Samantha Kerr <samantha.k@healthbridge.io>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: POC environment & connectivity timeline (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering)

Hi Alex / Samantha —

Great to meet last week. Per our conversation, attached is a first-pass mutual action plan for the POC environment so your engineers can validate model performance on a near-production setup. High-level ask: can HealthBridge commit to the connectivity items by the dates in the sheet so we can run a 2-week evaluation window starting 2026-09-02?

Key pieces in scope (short):
- Organization onboarding (tenant + admin invite) — Redwood issues org invite and initial admin API keys
- API keys / ephemeral tokens — we will provide scoped keys for ingestion and inference; you will provide a test account and sample payloads
- IP allowlist — HealthBridge to allow Redwood egress IPs listed in the network diagram (attachment)
- VPC peering — optional for dedicated path; if you want low-latency routing we’ll create a peering request and coordinate CIDR exchange

Please review the MAP_HealthBridge_v1.xlsx and the network diagram. I’ve included a compact timeline inside the sheet. If that looks good I’ll route the technical checklist to Marcus for implementation details.

Next steps (asks):
1) Confirm start window: ideally 2026-09-02 — respond by 2026-08-13
2) Assign one technical lead from HealthBridge for VPC/IP coordination (name + email)
3) Procurement note: we’ll need an SOW/PO for reserved capacity if you decide to proceed after eval — procurement address copied for visibility

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_HealthBridge_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_network_diagram.png (png), onboarding_checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Alex White <alex@healthbridge.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Kerr <samantha.k@healthbridge.io>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: POC environment & connectivity timeline (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering)

Thanks Jordan — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs from our side before we lock dates: 

- For the API keys you mentioned "scoped keys for ingestion and inference" — do you have an example policy for read/write/scoped privileges we can consume?
- For IP allowlist: we prefer a deterministic set (not a large CIDR range). Does Redwood publish a stable set of egress IPs when Dedicated isn't used?
- VPC peering: our network team prefers peering only after security review. Can we run the eval entirely over public egress + IP allowlist and then opt into peering in week 2 if latency requires it?

We can commit to the 2026-09-02 start window pending answers to the above and confirmation of our network lead (see below).

Technical lead: Marcus Lin (marcus.lin@healthbridge.io) — he’ll coordinate with your infra folks. Procurement: procurement@healthbridge.io for SOW/PO threads.

—Alex
Alex White
Head of Product | HealthBridge
alex@healthbridge.io

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex White <alex@healthbridge.io>
Cc: Samantha Kerr <samantha.k@healthbridge.io>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@healthbridge.io>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: POC environment & connectivity timeline (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering)

Alex — great questions, answered inline below. I’ve also attached a condensed checklist and example token policy.

- Scoped API policy: see onboarding_checklist.pdf, section "Scoped Key Template" — we provide a tokens.json example with separate keys for ingestion (limited to /ingest endpoints) and inference (limited to /generate). Tokens are short-lived by default; we can issue an "eval" key with 30-day TTL or ephemeral 1-hour tokens depending on your preference.

- Egress IPs: for hosted mode we publish a stable list of 8 egress IPs (see redwood_network_diagram.png). If you prefer not to maintain CIDR ranges we can do an allowlist by those IPs and a small ASN block; we’ll provide the exact list in a follow-up.

- Peering approach: yes — 100% fine to run the eval on hosted + IP allowlist for week 1 and then decide on peering in week 2. We recommend measuring median p95 latency in the first week and we’ll help instrument that.

I’ve pulled the high-level timeline into the message here: 
- 2026-08-13: HealthBridge confirms start window and tech lead (you did — Marcus)
- 2026-08-18: Redwood sends scoped API keys and sample payloads; HealthBridge to configure IP allowlist and verify connectivity
- 2026-08-25: Dry-run tests (small inference batch) to validate auth, payload schema, and latency telemetry
- 2026-09-02 to 2026-09-16: Evaluation window (2 weeks)
- 2026-09-20: Review checkpoint to discuss peering and next-phase sizing/SOW

Soojin will pick up procurement/credits/contracting threads, and Marcus (internal) can coordinate with your network team on the CIDR exchange.

I’ll follow with the egress IP list and an example tokens.json by end of day 2026-08-10.

Jordan

Attachments: onboarding_checklist.pdf (contains token examples and responsibilities), MAP_HealthBridge_v1.xlsx

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex White <alex@healthbridge.io>, procurement@healthbridge.io
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@healthbridge.io>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: POC environment & connectivity timeline (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering)

Hi Alex / Procurement team —

I’m looping in procurement so we can align on the quick SOW option for the eval and confirm credits for the 2-week window. Two quick procurement notes: 
1) We can issue an evaluation SOW that covers reserved capacity trial credits; if you want peering in week 2 that will be a separate attachment to the SOW.
2) If HealthBridge can provide a PO by 2026-09-01 we’ll prioritize dedicated slots for the evaluation window. Otherwise we’ll run on hosted capacity and guarantee baseline throughput per the MAP.

Marcus (cc) — Jordan indicated he’ll send the egress IP list and token templates; can you confirm your network schedule for the 2026-08-18 config step so we can book the dry-run?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call to close PoC logistics this week.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director of GTM | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199
